La travesía. Al llegar volando al borde: The crossing. When you fly to the edge of the town, or press Enter at an airfield, you choose a destination and how to get there. Then you fly for real: the tower gives you the wind and the heading, you climb to your level and cross the region. The autopilot does everything if you want, and the N key speeds up the trip. Enter tells you at any time how much is left.
Llegar. O aterrizas en el campo, con la: Arrive. Either you land at the airfield, with the tower guiding you, or you fly in low over the town and land wherever you like. With assisted landing, which is on by default, the aircraft descends and lines up on its own. By hand, descend to the altitude the tower tells you and keep the alignment clicks in the center.
Lo que pasa en el aire. Turbulencias, ot: What happens in the air. Turbulence, another aircraft at your altitude that you must give way to by climbing or descending, and storms that you can go around, fly over if your aircraft climbs high enough, or fly through. In rain there is more wind and more storms.

Travesía en vuelo. {k} y {k2} suben y ba: Flight crossing. {k} and {k2} climb and descend one hundred meters. {k3} and {k4} turn ten degrees. {k5} turns the autopilot on or off, which holds the heading and altitude on its own. {k6} tells you how much is left, the heading, the altitude, the wind and the fuel. {k7} speeds up the crossing or returns it to its own pace. {k8} repeats the last thing the tower said. {k9}, or {k10}, opens the flight menu: change destination, how you want to arrive and assisted landing. Without autopilot, two clicks tell you which way to turn: centered and high-pitched, you are lined up. A note plays when your altitude changes: the higher the pitch, the higher you are. Below {entero} meters the autopilot doesn't fly: the aircraft goes slower, uses more fuel and there are obstacles to jump, but the radar can't see you.
